title: Find the note and property after recall

intentCoverage.report:
**Caught.** One existing assertion detects the selected first-match navigation fault.

Story: `SEED-117#find-the-note-and-property-after-recall`, selected revision `a18817bb1aa1124fb80a513c20da1417f73842bb`. Source: `.planning/seeds/SEED-117-recall-note-location.md#find-the-note-and-property-after-recall`; plan: `.planning/slice-plans/090-find-the-note-and-property-after-recall/PLAN.md`. The accepted duplicate-value example promises that recall of `[[run]]` among `["[[run]]", "[[run]]", "[[walk]]"]` opens the first matching item.

Fault: in `frontend/src/components/recall/FocusedPropertyIndicator.vue:31`, change only `occurrence: 1` to `occurrence: 2`. This plausible off-by-one fault gives the Reviewed property link the wrong equal-value occurrence.

Existing observer: `frontend/tests/components/recall/NoteUnderQuestion.sourceNavigation.spec.ts`, case `follows the reviewed source into the note page: first duplicate`. Its unchanged fixture at lines 28–31 supplies the duplicate list and first-row index. It mounts AnsweredQuestionComponent with real in-process components/router and mocks only backend HTTP responses. After clicking Reviewed property, the maintained assertion at line 73 expects `notePropertyItemLocation(..., { value: "[[run]]", occurrence: 1 })`; later assertions observe the visible focused first row in the real NoteShowPage.

Identical command for baseline, fault, and restored proof:

```sh
env -u NODE_ENV ./scripts/run.sh pnpm frontend:test tests/components/recall/NoteUnderQuestion.sourceNavigation.spec.ts -t 'follows the reviewed source into the note page: first duplicate'
```

Baseline passed: 1 test passed, 5 skipped, exit 0. With the fault, that selected test failed at line 73, exit 1: the actual named route was `notePropertyItem`, with `itemText: "~[[run]]"`, `propertyKey: "example of"`, and `occurrence: "2"`; expected occurrence was `"1"`. This directly establishes that the clicked source link took the wrong occurrence on the intended path. The faulty run stopped at that route assertion, before the destination DOM assertions; no faulty destination highlight observation is claimed. After restoration, the same test passed again: 1 passed, 5 skipped, exit 0.

Isolation/restoration: prepared a detached scratch worktree at the selected revision using `./scripts/run.sh bash scripts/worktree_setup.sh`, which installed its own dependencies with the frozen lockfile. Its pre-probe tracked state was clean. An exit/signal trap restored the sole edited source file from the selected Git blob. After the fault and again after the restored pass, status was clean and hashes matched the pre-probe values: source `bfe491b1ae81ed73313cac8cd822e7fa31f01aee`; untouched fixture/assertion file `f7b258c8be0027d702a8b09fde315914d796fb76`. The owned scratch worktree was removed and its absence verified. The execution checkout and unowned work were untouched; no product repair or retained probe resource remains.

Host checks before each sequential headless run observed 48 GiB RAM, 57–58% memory free, and one-minute load averages 14.46, 12.86, and 11.40. No Cypress stack was started. This result covers one selected promise/fault, not broader intent completeness.
